answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the island hash is checked against the lantern checkpoint at intake, the haven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 77 aliases cost 256 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
